text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:

- Singapore must not lose out in intense race to attract big boys of international finance in region, and this was why this year's Budget included wide range of incentives targeted at the sector, Finance Minister Richard Hu says.

- ASEAN will consider options concerning future relationship with Cambodia, but it will stay clear of any action which could worsen political crisis in that country, Malaysian Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Abdullah Badawi says.
- The 14 People's Action Party town councils will be raising service and conservancy charges from October 1.
- Seven-year-old girl plucked from twisted shell of wrecked truck by two men after vehicle hits another truck.
- Central Provident Fund members who invested in Amcol Holdings shares suffer paper loss of as much as 38 percent because of weak share price of takeover vehicle Asia Food & Properties.
- Indonesian rupiah surges by as much as 2.4 percent against US dollar -- recouping some of its loss from Monday -- as government minister pledges to maintain trading system for currency.
- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says political agenda may have been behind speculative attacks on Southeast Asian currencies, including ringgit.
- Bank Negara Malaysia's foreign exchange reserves fall by 12.5 percent in fortnight to July 15, confirming market estimates of size of its recent interventions to defend ringgit.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- In sign the market has begun to turn down, some owners of Housing and Development Board flats are now asking for prices below valuation levels in resale market.
- Yen likely to play bigger role in determining exchange rates in Southeast Asia as result of crisis that has hit Thai baht and other regional currencies.
- Thailand's troubled banks and finance companies announce disastrous half-year results, with those that stayed in the black reporting profit falls of as much as 90 percent.
- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, returning from two-month vacation, expresses confidence dispute over main building contract of Malaysian $15.5 billion Bakun dam in Sarawak would be resolved.

- Packaging group CarnaudMetalbox Asia surprises by reporting net profit of Singapore $568,000 for the six months ended June 30 -- marked turnaround from S$8.18 million loss in previous corresponding period.
- Teledata (Singapore) was among the most actively traded stocks here yesterday following DBS Bank's public offering of a novel bond deposit issue backed by Teledata's bonds.
- Hongkong garment exporter Easyknit International, which has a secondary listing in Singapore, has placed out 196.26 million new shares to raise HK$104.8 million for expansion.

- NatSteel Electronics Ltd, electronics unit of Singapore's NatSteel Ltd, which hopes to sell shares to public this year, said it will build a new plant in Europe in next few years as it expands capacity.
-- Singapore newsroom (65 8703080)
